title: Boston College hockey to retire late Johnny Gaudreau's No 13 in pregame ceremony
text:
Gaudreau's jersey is the just the third that will be retired in Boston College hockey history

Hockey star killed in crash with illegal immigrant is remembered by sister

College hockey player Ryan O'Shea was killed in a tragic wrong way crash. Katherine O'Shea honors the legacy of her brother after he was killed in the crash involving a twice-deported illegal immigrant.

Boston College will retire the late Johnny Gaudreau’s No. 13 during a pregame ceremony on Feb. 12, 2027, the university announced Wednesday.

Gaudreau, nicknamed "Johnny Hockey," played at Boston College for three seasons (2011-14) and dominated during his tenure. He was a member of Boston College’s 2012 National Championship team as a freshman, led the nation in scoring as a junior and was awarded the 2014 Hobey Baker Award, which is presented to college hockey’s best player.

"We are proud to honor Johnny Gaudreau by retiring his No. 13 at Boston College," William V. Campbell Director of Athletics Blake James said in a statement. "Johnny was an extraordinary player who helped bring a national championship to the Heights and became one of the most accomplished players in our program's history. He will always hold a special place in the Boston College family."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Johnny Gaudreau #13 of the Columbus Blue Jackets takes a break during a stoppage in play against the Nashville Predators at Nationwide Arena in Columbus, Ohio, on March 9, 2024. (Getty Images)

In three years with the Golden Eagles, Gaudreau had a whopping 175 points — 78 goals and 97 assists — in 119 games played. In 2013-14, Gaudreau had 80 points, which was the most of any college hockey player since Peter Sejna’s 82-point performance with Colorado College in 2002-03.

Gaudreau’s No. 13 is just the third number Boston College has retired, alongside David Emma’s No. 16 and Mike Mottau’s No. 3. The Calgary Flames drafted Gaudreau in the fourth round of the 2011 NHL Draft, and he made his debut with them at the end of the 2013-14 season.

Johnny Gaudreau of the Boston College Eagles wins the 2014 Hobey Baker Memorial Award during a ceremony at the Loews Hotel in the Millennium Ballroom on April 11, 2014, in Philadelphia, Pa. (Getty Images)

In his 11-year career, during which he spent nine seasons with the Flames and two with the Columbus Blue Jackets, he recorded 243 goals and 500 assists, good for 743 points in 763 games played.

Gaudreau and his brother Matthew, who played four seasons at Boston College, were tragically killed in 2024 in New Jersey, where they were visiting for their sister’s wedding. The brothers were riding their bicycles in Salem County, New Jersey, when Sean M. Higgins allegedly hit and killed them. Johnny was 31 and Matthew was 29 at the time of their deaths.

Johnny Gaudreau #13 of the Boston College Eagles controls the puck against the Massachusetts Lowell River Hawks during the NCAA Division I men's ice hockey Northeast Regional Championship final at the DCU Center on March 30, 2014, in Worcester, Mass. (Getty Images)

Higgins pleaded not guilty on Jan. 25 and is facing multiple charges, including two counts of aggravated manslaughter. He is slated to go to trial in January 2027 after he rejected a plea deal.

On Tuesday, it was announced that the childhood rink where the Gaudreaus played will have a bronze statue memorializing the brothers.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.
